doc.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01

title: Brother John Marrero and how Marrero came to the banjo
summary: Marrero says his brother John, who played with Celestin, Piron, Oliver and others, started him on banjo; his mother played guitar and his father and brother bass; he moved from guitar through bass to banjo and drums.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did your father get you first or your brother?
My brother. Which one? John Marrera. You heard talk about John Marrera. He was a leading band you played.
Played with Solishtan a long time. John Marrera. With P. Ron too, didn't he? Yeah. He played with King Joe Oliver. You remember Joe Oliver? Yeah we had the records.

Yeah. And he played with Kid Rene and Buddy Pitty. And he started you on banjo. He started me on banjo. How I started banjo I picked it up to see my mother, she played guitar. My father was a bass player, which you heard about your knowledge. My brother was a bass player and my brother John was a guitar and a banjo player. But they all really was good and I used to listen to them all the time. And my first instrument was a guitar. My first number was Under the Double Eagle. I remember that and I can't play it now. You remember that? Under the Double Eagle? You remember that much? And I can't play it now, but it changed so many different keys. But I couldn't play it now. That's the time I remember. I used to play on a guitar. I used to play the guitar and I left guitar and I went to the bass violin. I started playing the bass violin. I started playing the bass violin. Then I went to the tenor banjo. And then the bandjo I dropped on my bass drum. I started playing the bass drum. So I've been fighting all of these things all the time. Mainly banjos. I used to play the bass drum all the time on the drums. Yeah? Yeah. So I played the record for Ohio State. Oh yeah? Yeah. I played the drum all day. On the records. I played the drums. I don't know.
